findings.claim: The render layer writes the 844×390 reference frame by hand 9 times across three files, though the token `tokens.safeArea.frame` holds it and `src/ui/layout.ts` already reads it. This breaks the CLAUDE.md rule against raw pixel sizes in src/. A later feature night could copy the literal or change one copy and miss the others (for example the outline width's /844 divisor vs the initial resolution uniform).
findings.evidence:
src/render/scene.ts:140-141 `let viewW = 844; let viewH = 390;`
src/render/scene.ts:213-214 `new Vector2(844, 390); applyViewport(initial.x || 844, initial.y || 390);`
src/render/camera.ts:85 `export function createCameraRig(width = 844, height = 390): CameraRig {`
src/render/materials/index.ts:147 `const resolution = { value: new Vector2(844, 390) };`
src/render/materials/index.ts:173 `widthPx.value = (OUTLINE_PX_AT_844 * Math.max(1, bufferWidth)) / 844;`
The token already exists: guardrails/design/tokens.json:68 `"safeArea": { "frame": [844, 390], ... }`, and src/ui/layout.ts:6 reads it: `const [frameW, frameH] = tokens.safeArea.frame;`
findings.suggestedFix: In each of the three files, import `tokens` from '@tokens' (car.ts already does this) and write `const [FRAME_W, FRAME_H] = tokens.safeArea.frame;`, or export it once from camera.ts and import it in scene.ts and materials. Then replace the 844/390 literals at the lines listed. The values are identical, so the camera, outline width and scene don't change.

confirmations.note: src/render/index.ts:5,8,9 still re-export frameWidthFor, LIGHT_DIRECTION, TOON_STEPS, attachOutline, groundMesh, outlinedFlatMesh, solidMesh and type RenderRole. A grep of tests/, harness/ and src/ finds no import of any of them through the index. PR #23 is no longer listed as in flight.

smoothNormals (geometry.ts:162), attachOutline and CREASE_ANGLE_DEG (outline.ts:84,19), and OUTLINE_PX_AT_844 and MaterialKind (materials/index.ts:36,20) are still exported. No file uses them outside their own module except the barrel's re-export of attachOutline.
outline.ts:47 and :57 still build the same `paletteAttribute(new Uint8Array(n).fill(paletteIndex('ink')))`.
props.ts:12 and track.ts:29 still declare `type Pt = [number, number]`. scene.ts:91 (was 87) spells out `[number, number][][]`.
The scene.ts:12 comment still reads 'body mesh + player ▼ marker'. car.ts:192-193 still adds the 'car-roundel' mesh.
